summary: Intermittent high inference latency during concurrent streams due to ephemeral socket exhaustion + retry bursts
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent spikes in end-to-end inference latency and occasional timeouts during periods of high concurrent streaming traffic. Symptoms are more pronounced after short bursts of requests and persist even when the serving runtime shows healthy token throughput.

Impact: Several user-facing features at NovaScribe experienced degraded responsiveness for ~5-30s windows, leading to user timeouts and feature degradation. No model correctness regressions observed.

Environment: Customer uses Redwood Dedicated cluster in us-east, SDK v1.3.2 (Node and Python clients), requests over TLS through API gateway. Dedicated pool sized according to contract and reporting normal GPU utilization in CloudWatch dashboards.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use SDK v1.3.2 with default client settings (maxConnectionsPerHost=2, aggressive retry strategy).
2) Start 30 concurrent streaming chat sessions that each send an initial prompt simultaneously.
3) Observe end-to-end latency for first token across sessions and any 504/timeout errors from the SDK.
4) Repeat with SDK config: increase pool to 8 and disable exponential retry to compare behavior.
logs:
Customer-provided SDK client logs (abridged): 
[2026-03-10T14:21:03Z] WARN request_retry: attempt=1 host=api.redwood.example.com queue_time_ms=324 context=stream-init
[2026-03-10T14:21:03Z] ERROR request_timeout: request_id=abc123 elapsed_ms=15000 status=timeout
[2026-03-10T14:21:05Z] INFO socket_status: opened=2 in_use=2 idle=0 total_attempts=18
[2026-03-10T14:21:30Z] WARN retry_backoff: backoff_ms=8000 attempts=3 jitter=0.0

Gateway logs show many simultaneous TLS handshakes followed by TCP TIME_WAIT spikes on gateway hosts during the window. Serving metrics do NOT show corresponding GPU saturation; token service QPS remains within expected range.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: problem originated in serving runtime. Validation: serving runtime metrics (latency and token throughput) stayed normal, GPUs not saturated.
Conclusion: issue likely client-side or gateway-level resource exhaustion leading to request queueing before reaching runtime.

Observed SDK defaults: maxConnectionsPerHost=2 and aggressive exponential backoff without jitter in v1.3.2. Under bursty concurrency, the SDK serialized pending requests behind the small connection pool; combined with long backoff windows and no jitter, many clients retried in lock-step (retry bursts), causing transient queueing and perceived latency spikes.

Additional contributing factor: short socket idle timeout at the gateway + high connection churn produced many sockets in TIME_WAIT, causing ephemeral port exhaustion on gateway frontends and increasing TLS handshake latency for new connections.
Reproduction verified in-house using synthetic load: with SDK default settings we reproduced 5–20s tail latencies and request timeouts; increasing pool and enabling jitter eliminated most spikes.
Telemetry: traces show requests spending majority of time in SDK-level client queueing (queued_ms) and time in TLS handshake rather than in serving runtime.
workaround: Customer applied temporary mitigations: updated SDK config to maxConnectionsPerHost=8 and reduced retry maxAttempts to 2 with randomized jitter; enabled HTTP keepalive and increased OS ephemeral port range on their gateway. This eliminated the immediate 5-30s spikes.
Recommendation to ops: add connection reuse and tune gateway TCP TIME_WAIT reuse to reduce churn until SDK patch deployed.
resolution: Root cause: combined client SDK connection pool small default and non-jittered exponential backoff produced synchronized retry bursts, which—together with gateway ephemeral socket churn—caused queuing and perceived inference latency. Serving runtime was healthy.

Fix implemented: SDK patch released in clientsdk v1.3.5 that increases default pool to 8 for dedicated-class customers, changes retry policy to use full jittered backoff by default, and exposes clear doc strings for pool/timeouts. Gateway-side guidance added to recommendations.
Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood/clientsdk/pull/3421
Customer status: NovaScribe upgraded to v1.3.5 and confirmed latency spikes resolved in production. Follow-up monitoring window of 72 hours completed with no recurrence.

Postmortem tasks: update QuickStart docs to call out pool and retry defaults for streaming workloads; add guidance to Dedicated onboarding checklist; create alert rule for SDK queue_time_ms exceeding 200ms in API gateway metrics.
